result:
Understood, and thanks for your patience. Before I write it up, there's one decision that's yours: **where this lives.** I haven't asked about that yet, and it shapes the whole design.

1. **Add it to the existing taproom app (my recommendation).** New pages and tables in the same Flask app and SQLite database on the Pi. You get one thing to run, back up and log into, and it follows the patterns the code already uses. The trade-off is that a bug in batch tracking could take the taproom tabs down on a busy night. I'd limit that risk by keeping the batch code in its own separate section of the app.

2. **A separate small app on the same Pi.** It gets its own database and its own address. A problem there can't touch the tabs. You'd have two things to keep running and back up, and some code would be duplicated.

3. **Off-the-shelf brewery software.** These packages already do lot tracing. But they're a monthly subscription, they'd sit apart from your Pi, and they'd make you work their way instead of the way you've described. I don't think they fit, but I'm naming the option so you can rule it out.

The sack scanner works the same with any of these. A cheap USB barcode scanner types into whichever page is open.

This is big enough for a proper written design. Once you pick, I'll write it up and save it in the project. A reviewer will read it before you do, and I may come back once with a few quick questions that only you can answer.

Which way do you want to go?
